audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers agree the chart is Trundle / Skill / Teemo / Teemo / Trundle / Teemo / Teemo, but the prose contradicts its own level 1: `early` opens "Teemo wins levels 1 through 3 cleanly" and whys[0] says "you cannot trade at level 1", while win[0] and phases[0].side both say Trundle.
audit.why: The chart card and the paragraph under it tell the player opposite things about the same stage. The chart is right: Chomp is a flat 3.5 seconds at every rank and Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank, so at level 1 Teemo can blank one bite and then owes you 3.5 seconds of nothing.
audit.corrected: Level 1 is Trundle's if he takes it; Teemo takes over from 2 once Toxic Shot is poisoning every auto.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] states the level-6 spike does not exist: "Subjugate offers no payoff against a squishy Teemo — he has almost no armor or MR to steal, so your R does near nothing and he simply blinds you and runs." whys[4] repeats it and `mid` puts a number on it: "he runs around 30 armor and 30 MR at level 6, so your R steals roughly 15 of each".
audit.why: Subjugate is not only a resistance steal. It also deals 20/25/30% of the target's maximum health as magic damage and heals Trundle for that same amount, half on cast and half over the following 4 seconds. Against Teemo's health bar that is the largest single chunk in Trundle's kit plus a full heal — the page is telling the player to leave his best button unpressed in the one lane where he needs it. The arithmetic is also wrong: the steal is 40%, so 30 armour gives 12, not 15.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is a real spike here: little resist steal, but a fifth of his max health as damage and the same again as healing, inside 650 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's central claim is that Teemo blinds every trade: spikes[0] "Teemo's Q blind fires the instant you step up", `early` "his Q blind fires faster than your Chomp", wants.foe[0] "Land Q blind before every Chomp", whys[5] "he still opens every trade with blind".
audit.why: Blinding Dart is a flat 7-second cooldown at all five ranks — ranking it up buys blind duration and nothing else. Chomp is a flat 3.5 seconds at all five ranks. Trundle gets two bites per blind and always has. The whole gameplan the page builds on top of this is therefore inverted: the trade Teemo wins is the one Trundle walks into with the blind already available, not every trade.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart 7s flat vs Chomp 3.5s flat — he blanks one bite in two. Step in after the dart, not before it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Teemo's move speed is called a passive in four places — spikes[1] "his move-speed passive refreshes", wants.you[2] "his passive move-speed kite", whys[1] "his move-speed passive", whys[5] "his move-speed kite" — and its actual switch-off condition appears nowhere.
audit.why: Move Quick is the W, 14 seconds flat, and Riot's own text says the passive speed lasts "until he is struck by an enemy champion or turret". One Chomp turns it off. That is the concrete reason Pillar of Ice works in this matchup and the page never says it. Only the active sprint survives being hit, and only for a few seconds.
audit.corrected: Move Quick (W, 14s): one hit from you switches off its passive speed. Only the sprint holds through damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] says Guerrilla Warfare lets him "enter camouflage". Riot's text says Invisible.
audit.why: Camouflage and Invisibility behave differently around control wards and true sight, so the word changes what a player thinks a pink ward buys him. Riot's description also gives the half nobody writes down: leaving it grants Element of Surprise, bonus attack speed for a few seconds — which is why the brush opener hits harder than the numbers suggest.
audit.corrected: Guerrilla Warfare: Invisible, and he leaves it with bonus attack speed.

audit.why: Toxic Shot and Blinding Dart are both magic damage, so Mercury's Treads plus Spirit Visage in report[8] is the right shape, and Doran's Shield into his poke is right. I left the item list alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and wants.you[2] attribute Iceborn Gauntlet's slow to "the Frost field from Chilling Path".
audit.why: Iceborn Gauntlet's slow field comes off its Spellblade proc. I could not find any item passive called Chilling Path, and item text is not in the kit library, so rather than assert a replacement name I rewrote both lines around Spellblade, which is verifiable.
sources: champ-data/_kits (item passives not covered — name removed rather than replaced)

audit.why: Both packet suspectNames here are false positives: "Frozen Domain's" is a possessive and "Use Pillar of Ice" is the correct ability name. Separately, the kit file's derived flags give Noxious Trap a knockup flag that Riot's own description does not support — shrooms slow and damage over time. I did not write a knockup anywhere.

edits.before: Teemo wins levels 1 through 3 cleanly because his Q blind fires faster than your Chomp, and the moment your auto is cancelled you have no trade pattern left — the AS steal never procs and the poison ticks back more than your passive heals. Do not step into his auto range to trade unless you can catch him mid-animation; instead last-hit with Chomp at its maximum range and accept that he gets free poke. Your only real threat in this window is landing Pillar behind him when he over-commits forward, which is rare — Teemo players know to stay at range and only step up on your cooldowns.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours if you take it: Chomp is a flat 3.5s at every rank and Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank, so he can blank one bite, not every bite. From 2 he pulls ahead, because Toxic Shot poisons every auto for 4 seconds and that ticks back more than King's Tribute heals off a dying wave. Do not walk into auto range with the dart available; last-hit at Chomp's 300 range and take the free poke. Your real threat in this window is Pillar of Ice behind him when he over-commits, which is rare — Teemo players step up on your cooldowns, not their own.

edits.before: Nothing materially changes at levels 4 through 6. Subjugate is almost worthless against Teemo: he runs around 30 armor and 30 MR at level 6, so your R steals roughly 15 of each — barely a rounding error while his blind still deletes your entire auto-based damage pattern. Play for wave control: shove him in under tower with Chomp when he walks up, call your jungler for a gank since Teemo has zero escape tools once he is caught mid-kite, and use Pillar to wall off his retreat if the jungler dashes in from river. Every death you hand him here is more valuable than any trade you can win.
edits.after: Nothing structural changes at levels 4 through 6, but Subjugate is not the dud this lane's reputation says. The steal is 40% of maybe 30 armour and 30 MR — twelve of each, a rounding error — but the same cast takes a fifth of his max health and heals you for every point of it, which on that health bar is a duel-ender. Play for wave control: shove him in with Chomp when he walks up, and call your jungler, because once Teemo is caught mid-kite he has only Move Quick's 14-second sprint. Pillar of Ice behind him seals the gank. Every death you hand him is worth more than any trade you win.

edits.before: This lane does not magically reverse — Teemo's shrooms make every side-lane push dangerous and his poison out-damages your sustain in prolonged skirmishes without a tank target to Subjugate. The honest win condition is: get your jungler involved early, stay even on CS, and accept that Trundle's real value in this game is team fighting — Subjugate their frontline, not Teemo. If you are even or slightly ahead, split-push with Iceborn Gauntlet's slow to threaten structures; never facecheck brush in the side lane at any point in the game.
edits.after: This lane does not magically reverse — shrooms make every side-lane push dangerous and Toxic Shot out-damages your sustain in prolonged skirmishes without a tank target to Subjugate. The honest win condition is: get your jungler involved early, stay even on CS, and accept that Trundle's real value in this game is team fighting — Subjugate their frontline, not Teemo. If you are even or slightly ahead, split-push with Iceborn Gauntlet's slow. Never facecheck brush: Guerrilla Warfare keeps him Invisible while he moves inside it, and he leaves it with bonus attack speed.

edits.after: Guerrilla Warfare lets him move Invisible inside brush and open with bonus attack speed — but Blinding Dart is 7s flat against a 3.5s Chomp, so level 1 goes to whoever steps up first, and that is you.

notes: The Blinding-Dart-beats-Chomp error is the same one the mirror found from Teemo's side, and it looks templated: any Trundle page claiming an enemy 'blinds every trade' or 'answers every Chomp' should be re-checked against Chomp's flat 3.5s. The 'Subjugate is worthless vs squishies' framing is likely templated too and is worth sweeping across every low-resistance enemy in Trundle's file — the max-health damage and the equal heal make R a duel-winner into exactly those champions. Iceborn Gauntlet's 'Chilling Path' passive is almost certainly not a real item passive; item text is outside the kit library so I removed the name rather than invent a replacement. Kit-file derived flags give Noxious Trap a knockup that Riot's description does not support — trusted the description.
